claims.claim: Making a small payment on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time, but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.
claims.note: A payment by the party to be charged toward principal or interest due on a promissory note starts a new period if the claim is not yet barred. Once barred, such a payment alone does not revive it. The statute specifies no minimum payment.

claims.claim: Signing something on an old debt does not restart the clock.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: What the person signed matters. A signed writing containing an acknowledgment or promise can affect the defense; a signature alone does not establish that it does.

claims.claim: The limit in the stated scenario is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The stated scope is limited to debts subject to a four-year period. Section 337 lists covered actions.

claims.claim: The four-year limit keeps running no matter what is paid or signed.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: Section 337 expressly allows extension under section 360.

claims.claim: You can safely make a payment.
claims.quote: and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: The assurance is contradicted for a qualifying promissory-note payment made before the claim is barred.

claims.claim: You can safely sign a payment plan.
claims.quote: unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby
claims.note: The draft gives this assurance without knowing whether the plan contains a qualifying acknowledgment or promise.

flags.text: The claim that the period cannot be extended conflicts with section 337(d)’s express reference to section 360.
The draft omits the distinction between a promissory-note payment made before the claim is barred and the same payment made afterward.
“No matter what you pay or sign” disregards the type of obligation, what the payment was for, and whether the writing contains an acknowledgment or promise.
“You can safely” pay or sign is a personal assurance not supported by the sources.
A reader could make a payment that starts a new period or sign a plan containing an acknowledgment or promise that weakens a limitations defense.

result.summary: The sources do not support the blanket assurance. A qualifying promissory-note payment can start a new period before the claim is barred, but that payment alone cannot revive an already barred claim. For a signed plan, the contents matter.
